newsitem.title: INDIA: India to offer 56 oil blocks under new policy.
newsitem.headline: India to offer 56 oil blocks under new policy.

text.p: India is offering 31 offshore and 25 onshore blocks for exploration and production of crude oil under its New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP), a Petroleum Ministry official said on Monday.
"The blocks will be announced in September," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.

However, documents obtained by Reuters show that 53 of the 56 blocks were offered earlier but were not bid for. Only three offshore blocks in Bombay, Krishna-Godavary and Saurashtra basins are new additions.
Most of the blocks in the NELP list have been offered more than twice, with some being included in earlier rounds since the Fourth Exploration Round in 1991.
The NELP round, which should have been announced in August, is behind schedule since a Petroleum Tax Code for facilitating investment in exploration is yet to be finalised.
"We are going ahead with the announcement in September. The brochure will specify that the tax code will be announced later," the official said.

The offshore blocks on offer are two in Andaman and Nicobar, four in Bengal, four in Bombay, five in Cauvery, six in Kerala-Konkan, three in Krishna-Godavari, three in Mahanadi, two in Palar, and one each in Saurashtra and Gujarat-Kutch basins.
The 25 onshore blocks are in Assam-Arakan, Arunachal Pradesh, Bengal, Gujarat- Kutch, Ganga Valley, Gondwana, Himalayan foothills, Mahanadi, Rajasthan, Spiti Zanskar and Vidhyan basins.

Incentives under the NELP include a five-year tax holiday extendible to seven years in northeastern India, the abolition of local tax, open availability of exploration acreages, ad-valorem royalty rates and no mandatory participation of state-run companies.
The royalty has been fixed at 10 percent for offshore blocks and 12.5 percent for onshore blocks.
